questions.question: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere is 4158 cm 2 . Find its volume (in cm 3 ).
questions.questionHtml: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere is 4158 cm<sup>2</sup>. Find its volume (in cm<sup>3</sup> ).
questions.solution:
⇒ 3 π r2 = 4158 cm2

⇒ r2 = (4158 × 7) ÷ 3 × 22 cm2

⇒ r2 = 9 × 49 cm2 ⇒ r = 21 cm

Now, Volume of hemisphere = 2/3 π r3

questions.question: How many spherical bullets, each bullet being 7 cm in diameter, can be made out of a cube of lead whose edge measures 77 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.questionHtml: How many spherical bullets, each bullet being 7 cm in diameter, can be made out of a cube of lead whose edge measures 77 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Given:

Edge of cube = 77 cm

Diameter of each bullet = 7 cm

Concept used:

Volume of a sphere = (4π/3) × r3

Calculation:

Radius of the spherical bullets = 7/2 = 3.5 cm

Let x numbers of bullets can be made

Now, volume of a spherical bullet = 4/3 × 22/7 × (7/2)3

According to the question,

4/3 × 22/7 × (7/2)3 × x = (77)3

⇒ x = (77 × 77 × 77 × 3 × 7 × 8)/(4 × 22 × 7 × 7 × 7)

⇒ x = 2541

∴ Total 2541 bullets can be made

questions.question: If the height and slant height of a right circular cone are 8 cm and 10 cm, respectively, then the volume of the cone is (use \(\pi=\frac{22}{7}\) ): (correct the two decimal places)
questions.questionHtml: If the height and slant height of a right circular cone are 8 cm and 10 cm, respectively, then the volume of the cone is (use \(\pi=\frac{22}{7}\)): (correct the two decimal places)
questions.solution:
Given:

The height and slant height of a right circular cone are 8 cm and 10 cm, respectively
Formula used:

Volume of the cone = \(\frac{1}{3}\pi \left( l^2- h ^2\right)h\), where 'l' and 'h' are the slant height and height of the cone.

Calculation:

Volume of the cone = \(\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{22}{7}\times \left ( 10^2 -8^2 \right)\times 8 = 301.71cm^3\)

∴ The volume of the given cone is 301.71 cm3

questions.question: A conical tent has a radius of 7 m and a vertical height of 24 m. How many full bags of rice can be emptied in it if the space occupied by the rice in each bag is 2 m 3 ?
questions.questionHtml: A conical tent has a radius of 7 m and a vertical height of 24 m. How many full bags of rice can be emptied in it if the space occupied by the rice in each bag is 2 m<sup>3</sup>?

Volume = 1/3 × 22/7 × 72 × 24

Volume = 1232 m3

Number of bags = 1232 / 2

Number of bags = 616

questions.question: A cylindrical vessel of diameter 32 cm is partially filled with water. A solid metallic sphere of radius 12 cm is dropped into it. What will be the increase in the level of water in the vessel (in cm)?
questions.questionHtml: A cylindrical vessel of diameter 32 cm is partially filled with water. A solid metallic sphere of radius 12 cm is dropped into it. What will be the increase in the level of water in the vessel (in cm)?
questions.solution:
Given:

The diameter of the cylindrical vessel = 32 cm

The radius of the solid metallic sphere = 12 cm

Formula used:

The volume of a cylinder = π × (Radius)2 × (Height)

The volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × (Radius)3

Calculation:

The radius of the cylindrical vessel = 32/2 = 16 cm

Let, the height of water increase = x cm

So, π × (16)2 × x = (4/3) × π × (12)3

⇒ 256x = 2304

⇒ x = 2304/256

⇒ x = 9

∴ The level of water in the vessel (in cm) will increase 9 cm

questions.question: The radius of the base of a solid right circular cone is 8 cm and its height is 15 cm. The total surface area of the cone is:
questions.questionHtml: The radius of the base of a solid right circular cone is 8 cm and its height is 15 cm. The total surface area of the cone is:
questions.solution:
r = 8 cm and h = 15 cm

As we know,

l2 = r2 + h2

l2 = 82 + 152

l2 = 64 + 225

l2 = 289

l = √289

l = 17

Total surface area of cone = πr (l + r) = π × 8 × (17 + 8) = π × 8 × 25 = 200 π

questions.question: A cuboid of sides 12 cm, 18 cm and 27 cm is melted to form a cube. What is the ratio of the total surface area of the cuboid to that of the cube?
questions.questionHtml: A cuboid of sides 12 cm, 18 cm and 27 cm is melted to form a cube. What is the ratio of the total surface area of the cuboid to that of the cube?
questions.solution:
Side3 = 12 × 18 × 27 ⇒ side = 3√(12 × 18 × 27) = 18

Total surface area of the cuboid  = 2( 12 x 18 + 18 x 27 + 12 x 27) =  2052

Total surface area of the cube = 6 x 18 x 18 = 1944

The ratio of the total surface area of the cuboid to that of the cube ⇒ 2052 : 1944 ⇒ 19 : 18

questions.question: The volume of a solid cylinder with height 6 cm is 231 cm 3 . The radius of the cylinder is∶
questions.questionHtml: The volume of a solid cylinder with height 6 cm is 231 cm<sup>3</sup>. The radius of the cylinder is∶
questions.solution:
Formula used:

Volume of cylinder = πr2h

where,

r = radius of cylinder

h = height of cylinder

Calculations:

Volume of cylinder = πr2h

⇒ 231 = (22/7) × r2 × 6

⇒ r2 = 231 × (7/22) × (1/6)

⇒ r2 = 12.25

⇒ r = √12.25

⇒ r = 3.5 cm

∴ The radius of the cylinder is 3.5 cm.

questions.question: What is the volume (in cm 3 ) of a spherical shell whose inner and outer radii are respectively 2 cm and 3 cm?
questions.questionHtml: What is the volume (in cm<sup>3</sup>) of a spherical shell whose inner and outer radii are respectively 2 cm and 3 cm?
questions.solution:
Given:

Inner radius (r) = 2 cm

Outer radius (R) = 3 cm

Formula used:

Volume of a hollow sphere of outer radius R and inner radius r = 4/3π(R3 – r3)

Calculation:

According to the question

Volume of a hollow sphere of outer radius R and inner radius r = 4/3π(R3 – r3)

⇒ 4/3 × π × (33 – 23)

⇒ 4/3 × π × (27 – 8)

⇒ 4/3 × π × 19

⇒ 76π/3

∴ Volume of spherical shell is 76π/3

questions.question: What is the difference in the volume (in cm 3 ) of a sphere of radius 7 cm and that of a cone of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm? (Use π = \(\frac{22}{7}\) )
questions.questionHtml: What is the difference in the volume (in cm3) of a sphere of radius 7 cm and that of a cone of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm? (Use π = \(\frac{22}{7}\))
questions.solution:
Given:

The radius of the sphere = 7 cm

The radius of the cone = 7 cm

The height of the cone = 10 cm

Formula used:

The volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × (Radius)3

The volume of a cone = (1/3) × π × (Radius)2 × Height

Calculation:

The difference in volume = [(4/3) × π × 73] - [(1/3) × π × 72 × 10]

= [(4/3) × (22/7) × 343] - [(1/3) × (22/7) × 49 × 10]

= [(7 × 22)/3] (28 - 10)

= (154/3) × 18

= 924 cm3

∴ The difference in the volume (in cm3) is 924 cm3

questions.question: A cylindrical candle, 14 cm in diameter and length 2 cm is melted to form a cuboid candle of dimensions 7 cm × 11 cm × 2 cm. How many cuboidal candles can be obtained?
questions.questionHtml: A cylindrical candle, 14 cm in diameter and length 2 cm is melted to form a cuboid candle of dimensions 7 cm × 11 cm × 2 cm. How many cuboidal candles can be obtained?
questions.solution:
Given:

Diameter of cylindrical candle = 14 cm

Height of cylindrical candle = 2 cm

Dimensions of cuboid candle = 7 cm × 11 cm × 2 cm

Formula used:

Volume of cylinder = πr2h

Volume of cuboid = l × b × h

Number of cuboidal candles = Volume of cylinder / Volume of cuboid

Calculations:

Radius of cylinder (r) = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm

Volume of cylinder = π × 72 × 2 = 22/7 × 49 × 2 = 308 cm3

Volume of cuboid = 7 × 11 × 2 = 154 cm3

⇒ Number of cuboidal candles = 308 ÷ 154

⇒ Number of cuboidal candles = 2

∴ 2 cuboidal candles can be obtained.

A hemisphere has 42 cm diameter.

Concept used:

Curved surface area = 2πr2

The total surface area = 3πr2

Calculations:

According to the question,

Radius of hemisphere = 42/2 = 21 cm

Now CSA of hemisphere

CSA = 2π(21)2 

⇒ CSA = 2(22/7)(441)

Now TSA of hemisphere

questions.question: The length, breadth, and height of a room are 10 m, 8 m and 6 m respectively. Find the cost of white washing the walls of the room and the ceiling at the rate of Rs. 7.50 per m 2 .
questions.questionHtml: The length, breadth, and height of a room are 10 m, 8 m and 6 m respectively. Find the cost of white washing the walls of the room and the ceiling at the rate of Rs. 7.50 per m<sup>2</sup>.
questions.solution:
Area of four walls of room = 2h (l + b)  = 2 × 6 (10 + 8) ⇒ 12 × 18= 216 m2

Area of ceiling = l × b = 10 × 8 = 80 m2

Total area of four walls and ceiling = 216 + 80 = 296 m2

Now, the cost of whitewashing the walls and ceiling = 296 × 7.50 = Rs.2,220

questions.question: A swimming pool is 40 m in length, 30 m in breadth and 2.2 m in depth. The cost of cementing its floor and the four sides at Rs. 25/m 2 is∶
questions.questionHtml: A swimming pool is 40 m in length, 30 m in breadth and 2.2 m in depth. The cost of cementing its floor and the four sides at Rs. 25/m<sup>2</sup> is∶
questions.solution:
Length of swimming pool = l = 40 m

Breadth of swimming pool = b = 30 m

Depth of swimming pool = h = 2.2 m

∴ Area of floor of swimming pool = l × b = 40 × 30 = 1200 m2

⇒ Area of four walls of swimming pool = 2(lh + bh) = 2(40 × 2.2 + 30 × 2.2) = 308 m2

⇒ Total area = 1200 + 308 = 1508 m2

⇒ Cost of cementing = 1508 × 25 = Rs. 37700

questions.question: How many small solid spheres each of 5 mm radius can be made out of a metallic solid cone whose base has radius 21 cm and height 30 cm?
questions.questionHtml: How many small solid spheres each of 5 mm radius can be made out of a metallic solid cone whose base has radius 21 cm and height 30 cm?
questions.solution:
Given:

The radius of the base of cone = 21 cm = 210 mm

The height of the cone = 30 cm = 300 mm

The radius of the sphere = 5 mm

Formula used:

The volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × (radius)3

The volume of a cone = (1/3) × π × (radius)2 × height

Calculation:

Let, the number of sphere required = x

So, x × (4/3) × (22/7) × (5)3 = (1/3) × (22/7) × (210)2 × 300

x × (4/3) × (22/7) × 125 = (1/3) × (22/7) × 44100 × 300

x × 4 × 125 = 44100 × 300

x = (44100 × 300)/(4 × 125)

x = 26460

∴ The total number of required solid spheres is 26460

questions.question: A 18 m deep well with diameter 7 m is dug and the earth from digging is spread evenly to form a platform 18 m × 14 m. The height of the platform is:

questions.question: The breadth of a room is twice its height and half its length. The volume of the room is 1728 m 3 . The length of the room is:
questions.questionHtml: The breadth of a room is twice its height and half its length. The volume of the room is 1728 m<sup>3</sup>. The length of the room is:
questions.solution:
Given:

The breadth of a room is twice its height and half its length. The volume of the room is 1728 m3.

Formula Used:

Volume (V) = Length (L) × Breadth (B) × Height (H)

Calculation:

Let the height be H. Then, breadth B = 2H and length L = 4H.

Given volume, V = 1728 m3

⇒ 1728 = L × B × H

⇒ 1728 = 4H × 2H × H

⇒ 1728 = 8H3

⇒ H3 = 1728 / 8

⇒ H3 = 216

⇒ H = ∛216

⇒ H = 6 m

Therefore, Length L = 4H = 4 × 6 = 24 m

∴ The correct answer is option (4).

Given:

Height = 7 cm

Curved surface area = 70π cm2

Formula Used:

Curved Surface Area = 2πrh 

Total surface area = 2πr(r + h) 

Where, r = radius, h= height of the cylinder 

Calculation:

Curved surface area = 70π

⇒ 2πr × 7 = 70π

⇒ r = 5 cm 

Now, Total surface area = 2πr(r + h)

⇒ 2 × π × 5 × (5 + 7)

⇒ 2 × π × 5 × 12 = 120π cm2 

Hence, the total surface area is 120π cm2.

questions.question: The height of a cylinder is 8 cm, and its area of the base is 20 cm 2 . Find its volume?
questions.questionHtml: The height of a cylinder is 8 cm, and its area of the base is 20 cm<sup>2</sup>. Find its volume?

options.html: 180 cm3
160 cm3
100 cm3

questions.solution:
Given:

Height (h) = 8 cm

Area of the base (A) = 20 cm2

Formula used:

Volume (V) = Area of the base (A) × Height (h)

Calculation:

V = 20 cm2 × 8 cm

⇒ V = 160 cm3

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: The circumference of the base of a cylindrical vessel is 44 cm and its height is 25 cm. How many liters of water can it hold? (Take \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\) )
questions.questionHtml: The circumference of the base of a cylindrical vessel is 44 cm and its height is 25 cm. How many liters of water can it hold? (Take \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\))
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Radius (r) = Circumference ÷ 2π = 44 × (7/44) = 7 cm.

Volume in cm3 = π × r2 × h = (22/7) × 72 × 25 = 3850 cm3.

Convert to liters (1 L = 1000 cm3): 3850 ÷ 1000 = 3.85 liters.

∴ The correct answer is 3.85 liters.

Alternate Method

Given:

Circumference of the base = 44 cm

Height of the cylinder (h) = 25 cm

Formula Used:

Circumference of base = 2πr

Volume of cylinder = πr2h

1 liter = 1000 cm3

Calculations:

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r = 44

⇒ (44/7) × r = 44

⇒ r = 44 × (7/44)

⇒ r = 7 cm

⇒ Volume of cylinder = (22/7) × (7)2 × 25

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 49 × 25

⇒ Volume = 22 × 7 × 25

⇒ Volume = 154 × 25

⇒ Volume = 3850 cm3

⇒ Capacity in liters = 3850 ÷ 1000 = 3.85 liters

∴ The correct answer is 3.85 liters.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

TSA = 2πr(r + h), where r is the radius of the base and h is the height.

Curved Surface Area of Cylinder

CSA = 2πrh. This represents the outer wall surface area, excluding the top and bottom circular faces.

Metric Volume Conversion

1 m3 = 1000 liters. Conversely, 1 liter = 1000 cm3 or 1000 ml.

questions.question: If the numerical value of twice the curved surface area of a right circular cylinder is equal to the numerical value of its volume, then what is the numerical value of the radius of the base of the cylinder?
questions.questionHtml: If the numerical value of twice the curved surface area of a right circular cylinder is equal to the numerical value of its volume, then what is the numerical value of the radius of the base of the cylinder?
questions.solution:
Let the radius of the base and height be R and H respectively.

According to the question,

2πRH × 2 = πR2H ⇒ R = 4 (∵ R ≠ 0 and H ≠ 0)

questions.question: Find the surface area (in m 2 ) of a cuboid that is 11 m long, 7 m broad and 4 m high.
questions.questionHtml: Find the surface area (in m<sup>2</sup>) of a cuboid that is 11 m long, 7 m broad and 4 m high.
questions.solution:
Given:

Length (l) = 11 m

Breadth (b) = 7 m

Height (h) = 4 m

Formula used:

Surface Area of a Cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl)

Calculation:

Surface Area = 2(11×7 + 7×4 + 4×11)

⇒ Surface Area = 2(77 + 28 + 44)

⇒ Surface Area = 2(149)

⇒ Surface Area = 298 m2

∴ The correct answer is option 3.

questions.question: Find the curved surface area (in cm 2 ) of a cone of radius 3 cm and height 4 cm.
questions.questionHtml: Find the curved surface area (in cm<sup>2</sup>) of a cone of radius 3 cm and height 4 cm.
questions.solution:
Given:

Radius (r) = 3 cm

Height (h) = 4 cm

Formula Used:

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cone = πrl

Where, l = slant height = \( \sqrt{ r^2 + h^2 } \)

Calculation:

l = \( \sqrt{ 3^2 + 4^2 } \)

⇒ l = \( \sqrt{ 9 + 16 } \)

⇒ l = \( \sqrt{ 25 } \)

⇒ l = 5 cm

CSA = π × r × l

⇒ CSA = π × 3 × 5

⇒ CSA = 15π cm2

∴ The correct answer is option 3.

questions.question: What is the volume of a sphere whose diameter is 16.8 cm? \(\rm[Use \ \pi=\frac{22}{7} ]\)
questions.questionHtml: What is the volume of a sphere whose diameter is 16.8 cm? \(\rm[Use \ \pi=\frac{22}{7} ]\)

options.html: 2487.312 cm3
2473.812 cm3
2483.712 cm3
2483.172 cm3

questions.solution:
Formula used:-

Volume = \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\)

Calculation:-

Diameter = 2 × radius(r)

radius = 8.4 cm

Volume = \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\)

Taking r = 8.4cm and \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\)

Volume = \(\frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7}\times (8.4)^3\)

Volume = 2483.712 cm3

The volume of the sphere is 2483.712 cm3

questions.question: How many metres of 2-m-wide cloth will be required to make a conical tent with a diameter of the base as 14 m and slant height as 9 m? (ignore wastage)
questions.questionHtml: How many metres of 2-m-wide cloth will be required to make a conical tent with a diameter of the base as 14 m and slant height as 9 m? (ignore wastage)
questions.solution:
Let the length of the cloth be a, then  area of cloth = a × 2 = 2a m2

Diameter of tent = 14 m, then Radius of tent = 14/2 = 7 m, Slant height = 9 m

Curved surface area of cloth = 22/7 × 7 × 9 = 198 m2 Then, ⇒ 2a = 198 ⇒ a = 99 m

questions.question: The areas of three adjacent faces of a cuboid are 30 cm 2 , 20 cm 2 and 24 cm 2 . The volume of the cuboid is:
questions.questionHtml: The areas of three adjacent faces of a cuboid are 30 cm<sup>2</sup>, 20 cm<sup>2</sup> and 24 cm<sup>2</sup>. The volume of the cuboid is:

options.html: 120cm3
180 cm3
150 cm3

questions.solution:
Given:

Area of three adjacent faces of a cuboid are 30 cm2, 20 cm2, and 24 cm2

Formula used:

Area of rectangle = length × breadth

Volume of cuboid = length × breadth × height

Calculation:

Area of three adjacent faces of cuboid are lb, bh, lh

where l →  Length of cuboid

b → Breadth of cuboid

h → Height of cuboid

According to question,

lb = 30, bh = 20, lh = 24

Now, lb/bh = 30/20

⇒ l/h = 3/2

⇒ l = (3/2) × h      ----(i)

lh = 24      ----(ii)

Putting value of l from (i) in (ii)

(3/2) × h × h = 24

⇒ h2 = 16 

⇒ h = 4 cm

l = (3/2) × 4 = 6 cm

b = 30/6 = 5 cm

Volume of cuboid = lbh = 6 × 5 × 4 = 120 cm3.

∴ Volume of cuboid is 120 cm3.

Shortcut Tricklb = 30; bh = 20; lh = 24

(lbh)2 = 30 × 20 × 24

so the volume of cuboid = lbh = 120 cm3
